examples: This rickety beater of a car isn’t worth repairing anymore.
He found going to the Edinburgh Castle was worth it.
I think you’ll find my proposal worth your attention.

senses.definition: Making a fair equivalent of, repaying or compensating.
examples: This job is hardly worth the effort.

senses.definition: Value.
examples: I’ll have a dollar's worth of candy, please.
They have proven their worths as individual fighting men and their worth as a unit.
Stocks having a worth of two million pounds; £2 million worth of stock.

senses.definition: Having worth, merit, or value.
Admirable or honourable.
Deserving, or having sufficient worth.
Suited; suitable; befitting.
Used to form the "anterior future", or "future in the past", indicating a futurity relative to a past time.
examples: On my first day at University, I met the woman who would become my wife.
Hi! I thought I'd come over and introduce myself. My name’s Chema.
I'm really flattered you would call your daughter after me.

senses.definition: Used to, did repeatedly, habitually; indicates an action that happened several times in the past (cannot describe continuous states, as in I used to live in London).
examples: When we were younger, we would cycle out to the beach most summer Sundays.

senses.definition: Was or were determined to; indicating someone's insistence upon doing something.
examples: I asked her to stay in with me, but she would go out.

senses.definition: Used as the auxiliary of the simple conditional modality, indicating a state or action that is conditional on another.
examples: If I won the lottery, I would give half the money to charity.
I'd never do anything that went against my conscience.

senses.definition: Would not (negative auxiliary).
examples: Wouldn't you often have supper on the terrace on Sundays?

senses.definition: An injury, such as a cut, stab, or tear, to a (usually external) part of the body.
An injury to a person by which the skin is divided or its continuity broken.
A hurt to a person's feelings, reputation, prospects, etc.
examples: It took a long time to get over the wound of that insult.

senses.definition: To hurt or injure (someone) by cutting, piercing, or tearing the skin.
examples: The police officer wounded the suspect during the fight that ensued.

senses.definition: Suffering from a wound, especially one acquired in battle from a weapon, such as a gun or a knife.
examples: A wounded soldier.
The wounded lay on stretchers waiting for surgery.
Every single hospital was taking in wounded from the front.

senses.definition: Suffering from an emotional injury.
examples: My wounded pride never recovered from her rejection.

senses.definition: Of a particle: having undergone an inelastic collision.
examples: A wounded nucleon.

senses.definition: An indication of excitement, surprise, astonishment, or pleasure.
examples: Wow, I sure was surprised!

senses.definition: An expression of amazement, awe, or admiration.
examples: Wow! How do they do that?

senses.definition: Used sarcastically to express disapproval of something.
examples: Wow… good job using all of our supplies on the first day.

senses.definition: To amaze or awe.
examples: He really wowed the audience.

senses.definition: To enclose (an object) completely in any flexible, thin material such as fabric or paper.
examples: Christmas gifts are commonly known to be wrapped in paper.

senses.definition: To enclose or coil around an object or organism, as a form of grasping.
examples: A snake wraps itself around its prey.

senses.definition: To conceal by enveloping or enfolding; to hide.
To finish shooting (filming) a video, television show, or movie.
examples: To avoid going over budget, let's make sure we wrap by ten. (compare wrap up 2).

senses.definition: Encased in a wrapping.
A feature on a website or online service that includes a summary of a user's activity on the service during a given year, created by logging the user's personal data.
examples: Our wrappeds this year are so similar.
Why does YouTube have a wrapped now?

senses.definition: A sport where two opponents attempt to subdue each other in bare-handed grappling using techniques of leverage, holding, and pressure points.
The act of one who wrestles; a struggle to achieve something.
The complex joint between forearm bones, carpus, and metacarpals where the hand is attached to the arm; the carpus in a narrow sense.
examples: With a flick of the wrist, he threw the frisbee to a team-mate.

senses.definition: A stud or pin which forms a journal.
To hit a wrist shot.
To form letters, words or symbols on a surface in order to communicate.
examples: The pupil wrote his name on the paper.
Your son has been writing on the wall.

senses.definition: To be the author of (a book, article, poem, etc.).
examples: My uncle writes newspaper articles for The Herald.

senses.definition: To compose and send written information (to).
examples: Please write to me when you get there.
Please write me when you get there.
He never phones me, but he does write occasionally.

senses.definition: To compose and send (written information or a written message, e.g. a letter) to.
examples: Please write me a letter. Please write a letter to me.

senses.definition: A person who writes, or produces literary work; an author can refer to themselves as "the writer".
examples: Has your girlfriend written you another letter already? She’s quite a writer!
I met some of my favourite authors at the writers' convention.
The present writer (referring to oneself as the writer).

senses.definition: Anything that writes or produces output.
A machine or tool used for writing, often by chording keys on a specialized keyboard (e.g. braillewriter, microwriter, stenograph).
The seller of an option.
Graphism of symbols such as letters that express some meaning.
Something written, such as a document, article or book.
The process of representing a language with symbols or letters.
A work of an author.
examples: Congrats, you did an interesting piece of writing.

senses.definition: Of, relating, or characteristic of writing (i.e., of that which has been written).
examples: Written language is a way of representing spoken language.

senses.definition: Having been written.
examples: I can speak Japanese fairly well, but I have no understanding whatsoever of written Japanese.

senses.definition: A rap that was written in advance, as opposed to a freestyle.
Incorrect or untrue.
examples: Some of your answers were correct, and some were wrong.

senses.definition: Asserting something incorrect or untrue.
examples: You're wrong: he's not Superman at all.

senses.definition: Immoral, not good, bad.
examples: It is wrong to lie.

senses.definition: Improper; unfit; unsuitable.
examples: A bikini is the wrong thing to wear on a cold day.
